comments.body:
## RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 — confirmed)

**Mechanism.** `tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py:21` and
`tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py:21` do
`from tests.unit import _audit_page_helpers as H`. Neither `tests/__init__.py` nor
`tests/unit/__init__.py` exists, so `tests` can only resolve as a PEP-420 *namespace*
package — which requires the **repository root** to be on `sys.path`. Nothing in the test
harness puts it there:

* pytest's prepend import mode inserts only the first ancestor without `__init__.py`, i.e.
  `tests/unit` — not the repo root.
* `tests/conftest.py:39-40` deliberately inserts only `tests/` ("Make tests/ importable …
  regardless of pytest's import mode").

Repo root lands on `sys.path` only as a side effect of `python -m pytest` inserting the cwd.
The **bare `pytest` console script is the project's canonical invocation** (`Makefile:215`
`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q`; CI
`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:594` `pytest -m "not integration and not external"`),
and it does not.

**Discriminating experiment** (worktree at `origin/main` c89a2ddcc4, py3.12, `[ui]` extra
installed, cwd `/tmp` so the repo root cannot leak onto `sys.path`):

```
$ pytest /…/rebar-a371/tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py -q -p no:randomly
tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py:21: in <module>
    from tests.unit import _audit_page_helpers as H
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests'
1 error in 0.22s

$ (cwd=repo root) python -m pytest tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py -q -p no:randomly
1 passed in 1.98s
```

Identical for `test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py`. The single variable that flips the result
is whether the repo root is on `sys.path` — which rules out the alternatives (a missing
`[ui]` dependency, a conftest ordering problem, or an `importorskip` interaction): both runs
used the same interpreter, same installed extras, same conftest chain.

**Masking.** The two `pytest.importorskip` calls on lines 19-20 sit *above* the broken import
(hence the `# noqa: E402`), so in the lean CI suite the module skips before line 21 executes.
The modules read as covered while providing zero coverage in exactly the environment where
`[ui]` is present.

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** The behaviour violates the project's own canonical test invocation
(`Makefile:215`, `_build-and-test.yml:594`) — under it these modules fail at collection.

**Caller-dependency sweep:** `_audit_page_helpers` is imported by exactly these two modules
(repo-wide grep). No behavioural dependants; the fix is confined to the import form.

**Repo-wide scan:** these two lines are the only `tests.`-rooted imports under `tests/`
(the one other grep hit, `tests/scripts/reducer/test_reducer_links.py:533`, is prose in a
comment).

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

Found by the ticket-c5b3 sibling sweep after the same bug broke CI there.

`tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page.py:21` and `tests/unit/test_audit_ticket_page_heldout.py:21`
both do:

    from tests.unit import _audit_page_helpers as H  # noqa: E402

`tests` is not an importable package: neither `tests/__init__.py` nor `tests/unit/__init__.py`
exists. A `tests.`-rooted absolute import therefore only resolves when the repository root
happens to be on `sys.path`, which is true under `python -m pytest` (it inserts the cwd) and
FALSE under the bare `pytest` console script that CI runs. Demonstrated on ticket c5b3 with an
identical import:

    pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_scc_module_size_reconciliation_heldout.py
      -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tests'
    python -m pytest <same file>
      -> passes

## Why it is not failing today

It is MASKED, not correct. Both modules call `pytest.importorskip("fastapi")` and
`pytest.importorskip("httpx")` on the two lines ABOVE the import (hence the `# noqa: E402`).
The `[ui]` extra is absent from the lean CI suite, so the module skips before the broken
import line is ever executed. Install the `[ui]` extra and run bare `pytest` and these two
modules fail at collection.

That makes this worse than a plain breakage: the tests read as covered while providing no
coverage in exactly the environment where the extra IS present.

## The fix

`_audit_page_helpers.py` lives in `tests/unit/`, the same directory as both importers, so the
repo's established same-directory bare-name convention applies:

    from _audit_page_helpers import ...

pytest's prepend import mode inserts `tests/unit` into `sys.path` (it is the first ancestor
without an `__init__.py`), so a bare name resolves. Every other bare-name test import in this
repo is same-directory like this -- `metrics_polyglot_support`, `reviewbot_convergence_support`,
`_dc_support`, `test_completion_gate`.

Alternatively, move the helpers to `tests/_audit_page_support.py`: `tests/` is on `sys.path` by
DELIBERATE guarantee (`tests/conftest.py` inserts it), which is the mechanism c5b3 used for its
cross-directory case via the new `tests/module_size_support.py`.

## Why it was not fixed inside c5b3

c5b3 is an scc-metrics bug fix. These two files are an unrelated feature area (the audit page,
story ff6f), the defect cannot currently fire, and editing them there would have been scope
creep on a change already at its third patch set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Neither audit-page test module uses a `tests.`-rooted import.
- [ ] Both modules import and collect successfully under BARE `pytest` (not just
      `python -m pytest`) with the `[ui]` extra installed, verified from a cwd other than the
      repository root.
- [ ] A repository-wide check confirms no `tests.`-rooted import remains anywhere under
      `tests/`; consider a lint rule or a guard test so the pattern cannot return, since the
      failure is invisible under the common `python -m pytest` invocation.
compiled_state.title: audit-page tests use a 'tests.'-rooted import that cannot resolve under bare pytest
